P.label: shipped Palimpsest host, long-lived principal, journal carrier, delegation, update + cold resume

Q1.quote: The adjacent inspection room is 16°C and 45% RH. This is inside Filmtek's 15–20°C and 40–50% RH operating range. ... nitrate to leave the cold store in batches of up to 40 reels for at most 30 minutes, including scanning time.

Q2.quote: Complete the per-reel orphan-works rights risk assessment in January, scan at Northgate between 2 and 20 February ... and publish by 15 April 2026.

Q3.quote: There is no written permission, the estate's solicitor says a decision is unlikely before autumn 2026, and a verbal assurance is not sufficient for publication.

Q4.quote: TOTAL | 84,000 | Within the £84,000 grant; C2 Filmtek 15 days at £1,200 = £18,000; C3 transport £3,600; E1 contingency £4,620.

Q5.quote: The 2025 open day drew 2,340 visitors. ... That is the figure to use for the newsletter. ... This figure is not in the January pack.

Q6.quote: Project update, 20 January 2026 ... B scanning moved forward to 2–20 February, with 23–27 February as buffer ... the inspection room is available for scanning only until 28 February 2026.

Q7.quote: The delegated finding aligns with the plan's key judgement and confirms the three-week Filmtek booking. I have tightened deliverables/plan.md so the calibration assumption explicitly reflects it: Planning range: 20–30 minutes per reel end-to-end.

Q8.quote: The pack gives durations and vendor rates but not staff rates, page counts, scan cycle times or item-level throughput. The following assumptions are explicit so that they can be tested... calibrate on 13 February; if the inspection room moves outside 15–20°C or 40–50% RH, scanning stops.

notes: Q1 was solved by the principal from the pack; the delegated question was the per-reel scan time that the pack does not state.

The principal also used web_search and web_fetch for scan throughput. The finding and the web search are not independent, so causal attribution of the throughput assumption to the delegation alone is not exclusive.

The plan's throughput assumption (1 reel per 30-minute batch, 16 reels/day, 15 days, three-week booking) is traceable to the delegated 20-40 minute range, but the plan does not name the delegation as its source; it says 'Industry practice suggests'.

S.label: strong single-agent file baseline; prior findings in sources/prior-notes.md; native subagents disabled

Q1.quote: The inspection room is 16°C and 45% RH, inside Filmtek's 15–20°C and 40–50% RH range. ... Batches stay within the policy limit of 40 reels and 30 minutes door-to-door.

Q2.quote: Collection B assessment runs 12–30 January (15 staff days), producing a per-reel register ... publication is signed off only when every reel has a completed record.

Q3.quote: the only written legal advice says the Harrow estate is unlikely to decide before autumn 2026, and a verbal "spring" assurance cannot satisfy a donor restriction that requires written permission.

Q4.quote: The budget is £84,000 exactly: £79,780 committed and £4,220 (5.0%) held as contingency.

Q5.quote: This figure is already recorded in the Partnership's programme notes and should be used as stated in the newsletter. It is not a figure that requires external checking.

Q6.quote: not exercised: S was a one-shot baseline and did not receive the phase-2 project update

Q7.quote: not applicable: no independent result was delivered

Q8.quote: At an assumed average of about three minutes per reel at scan speed, a compliant batch is seven reels, giving four batches and 28 reels per day. This is the basis for the Filmtek booking ... These are planning rates, not guarantees.

notes: Q8 is the differentiator: the 3-minute-per-reel assumption is labelled but not stress-tested; the plan has no sensitivity path for a slower scanner and no go/no-go tied to the 30-minute rule.
The plan schedules B at Northgate on 9-20 March. It did not know the later booking change; that is a design limitation of the one-shot baseline, not a plan error on its own basis.

F.label: native DSH collaboration baseline; the installed subagent/workflow tools enabled; one spawned subagent

Q1.quote: The inspection room is at 16°C and 45% relative humidity, inside Filmtek's 15–20°C and 40–50% operating envelope. Reels remain in the 4°C cold store except during batches of no more than 40 reels and no more than 30 minutes, including scanning time.

Q2.quote: A documented rights risk assessment is completed for every reel in January–February, before any publication.

Q3.quote: The plan therefore does not schedule C for publication and commits no grant to C. ... a hard decision gate is set for 31 March 2026.

Q4.quote: The committed budget is £80,795, leaving £3,205 of the £84,000 ceiling unallocated and a £7,345 contingency (10% of direct costs).

Q5.quote: 2,340 visitors. ... The figure has no effect on the delivery schedule or budget; it is a communications input, not a planning constraint.

Q6.quote: not exercised: F was a one-shot baseline and was stopped before any phase-2 update

Q7.quote: not applicable to the Palimpsest rubric; the native subagent audit is the baseline's own cross-agent mechanism

Q8.quote: The single biggest technical unknown is Filmtek's actual per-reel scan time, which the pack does not state. The plan assumes 15 minutes per reel including handling ... if a reel takes 16–30 minutes, only one reel fits per batch and B needs about 22 days ... costing about £12,000 more ... if a reel takes more than 30 minutes, it cannot be completed within one compliant batch at all.

notes: The run was stopped when the campaign token cap was crossed; the plan is a real artifact but was still being edited. The score is provisional and the run is labelled truncated.

The native subagent produced a red-team audit that identified the per-reel scan time as the blocking unknown; the principal incorporated it into a sensitivity table and a go/no-go test. That is genuine native cross-agent influence and the strongest competitor observed.

I1_source_read.evidence: the branch session read sources/brief.md, sites.md, vendors.md, condition.md, collections.csv, open-questions.md and rights.md (glob + 7 reads, 9 calls, 21,573 tokens)

I2_finding.evidence: the branch statement states the inspection-room conditions, the 40-reel/30-minute rule and the absence of a throughput specification, and names the external 20-40 minute range as calibration rather than as pack fact

I3_settlement.evidence: delegation status COMPLETED, 'the research branch closed with an admitted conclusion'

I5_decision.evidence: the principal's delivery turn says the finding confirms the three-week Filmtek booking and it tightened the calibration assumption to 20-30 minutes per reel; the plan's 1-reel/30-minute batch, 16 reels/day and 15-day booking follow that assumption. The principal also web-searched the same question, so the finding is not the only cause.

I6_matched_control.evidence: P-minus was not run: the campaign reached its 25M-token cap before it could start. S is a weaker no-delegation comparison (single agent, no journal).

C2_stale.evidence: after the Northgate booking update the resumed principal moved B scanning to 2-20 February and treated the room as available only to 28 February; it did not keep the old March schedule

C3_irrelevant.evidence: the 2,340 open-day figure was correctly confined to the newsletter and never drove a programme decision; however, no independent irrelevant result was delivered and ignored

C4_uncertain.evidence: the estate's conflicting signals were preserved and C was excluded from the commitment; however, the uncertain question was not delegated and no uncertain delivered result was tested

C5_no_fabricated_authority.evidence: the branch result is labelled cell-local exploratory; the plan treats the scan rate as an assumption; no Evidence, Proof, Project Verification or ProjectIR revision was claimed

hypotheses.H3-SYN: SUPPORTED (bounded): one real independent finding was consumed and changed a load-bearing planning assumption. Not a statistical claim.
hypotheses.H3-COMP: SUPPORTED: the shipped host composed the branch port, frozen snapshot, reasoning store, activation and delivery with no new runtime.
hypotheses.H3-ACT: SUPPORTED: in the scored task the principal naturally called palimpsest_delegate for the throughput question, without being told which tool to call.
hypotheses.H3-CUR: PARTIALLY SUPPORTED: applicable and stale handled; irrelevant and uncertain were handled as project material but not as delivered results.
hypotheses.H3-VALUE: NOT ESTABLISHED: the native DSH baseline matched the decision quality and produced a stronger risk analysis at lower cost; Palimpsest was the most expensive condition.
hypotheses.H3-RELIABILITY: PARTIALLY SUPPORTED: palimpsest_begin refused honestly; no fabricated completion; existing tests cover duplicate, interrupted and new-basis behaviour; no live interrupted-delivery test was run.

budget.overrunCause: the F baseline was far more verbose than estimated; it was stopped as soon as the cap was detected
budget.note: Counts are reported model usage from the session streams, not billing. The cap was crossed; this is reported as a protocol violation and no counter was reset.

limitations: One run per condition; no statistical claim.
P and F used different research mechanisms and the F run was truncated
P-minus was not run because the token cap was reached; the matched no-delegation control is missing.
S and F are one-shot and did not receive the phase-2 update; currentness is a within-P observation, not a cross-condition comparison.
The evaluator, the participant and the model family share one machine; isolation is organizational, not blinded.
The principal used web_search/web_fetch, so the delegated finding's causal contribution to the throughput assumption is not exclusive.
